Subject: DPA redlines - archival handoff and deletion of snapshots

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached are the DPA redlines our legal team flagged. Two items they asked us to clarify and/or negotiate before we proceed: 1) "archival handoff" — where and when data moves to cold/long-term storage and whether those copies can cross borders; and 2) deletion of historical snapshots/backups — we need a contractual guarantee that when Aurum issues an erasure request, snapshots and any offsite archives will be purged or rendered inaccessible within a defined window.

Specifically, they want: a clear definition of "archival handoff" in the DPA, confirmation that primary customer data remains in-region, and an archival deletion SLA that covers snapshots and immutable backups. Can you confirm Redwood's default behavior and whether you can accept our proposed redline (see §4.3 in the attached PDF)?

We aim to close this this week if possible. Happy to jump on a short call.

Thanks,
Samantha

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DPA redlines - archival handoff and deletion of snapshots

Samantha —

Thanks for sending this along and for the clear asks. High-level summary of Redwood's defaults and initial position below; happy to iterate into DPA text.

1) Archival handoff (definition)
- Default behavior: Primary, actively served data is stored in the customer-selected region (by default, US regions for your account).
- Cold/archival snapshots: By default we persist weekly point-in-time snapshots in the same region for 90 days in our cold tier. For DR purposes we maintain a geographically separated replica (cross-region) for up to 365 days unless the customer elects a no-cross-border-archives option.
- Proposed DPA language: define "archival handoff" as the automated promotion of a time-bound snapshot to Redwood cold-tier storage (described in Appendix A), and state whether cross-region replication applies.

2) Deletion of snapshots & immutable backups
- Operational practice: When a valid erasure request is received, active data is removed from the serving layer within 72 hours. For cold snapshots, we render snapshots inaccessible and schedule deletion. For the cross-region replica, we target permanent removal within 45 days from request issuance for standard plans. Immutable backups (tape-style immutable copies retained for compliance) may require longer windows; we propose an explicit carve-out and a contractual timeline.

3) Practical options for Aurum
- No-cross-border-archives add-on: prevents cross-region replication; increases RPO mitigation fee.
- Expedited archival purge: paid option to accelerate permanent deletion of cold snapshots and replicas to a 14-day target. Includes an erasure certification.
- Certified archival erasure: for on-prem or private deployments we can provide a 30-day certified purge path tied to the Private deployment package.

Next steps I suggest: I will draft precise DPA wording for §4.3 and Appendix A that (a) defines archival handoff, (b) states default retention windows, and (c) offers the two contractual options above (no-cross-border / expedited purge). Can we schedule a 30m call today or tomorrow to align on acceptable timelines?

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Director, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

Markus — quick internal notes before we reply with contract language.

1) Commercial impact: the "no-cross-border-archives" option should be priced; it reduces DR flexibility and increases ops burden. Recommend we present it as an optional add-on with a one-time configuration fee + 10% recurring.

2) Operational feasibility: 45 days for cross-region purge is aggressive but doable for soft-delete workflows; immutable backups will likely need a longer explicit exception (e.g., 365 days) unless customer wants to pay for expedited destruction. Ensure we involve infra/SRE for the mechanics.

3) Sales play: offer expedited purge (14 days) as part of our Dedicated or Private customers only; for hosted customers, offer it as a paid premium.

4) Drafting: I'll bake those options into a short clause and an Appendix A that maps each storage tier to deletion timelines. Markus — can you own the DPA wording and attach the recommended appendix? Irene — please feed in any evidentiary / certification language (what we can commit to log-wise and the deletion attestation).

-Lauren

Subject: RE: DPA redlines - archival handoff and deletion of snapshots (proposed language + next steps)

Samantha — thanks again. Per our internal alignment, attached is a suggested redline bundle that (1) defines "Archival Handoff" and associated storage tiers, (2) maps retention and deletion windows, and (3) lists optional contractual add-ons (No Cross-Border Archives; Expedited Archival Purge; Certified Erasure for Private deploys). Highlights:

- Default: weekly snapshots retained in-region (cold tier) for 90 days; cross-region replica retained for DR up to 365 days (unless No Cross-Border opted).
- Erasure request handling: active/serving data removal within 72 hours; cold snapshots rendered inaccessible immediately and scheduled for permanent removal with the following targets: 45 days (standard), 14 days (expedited paid option), 30 days (Private deployment certified erasure).
- Evidence: for any deletion we can provide a deletion certificate referencing job IDs, timestamps, and affected snapshot identifiers. See Appendix A for the job ID schema.

Please review the attached PDF (redwood-dpa-proposed-redlines.pdf). If this looks acceptable we can update your DPA and route to your legal team for sign-off. Alternatively we can hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow 11:00am PT to walk through.

Best,
Markus Klein
